named.name: Cumene process (industrial preparation of phenol)
named.eq: C6H5-CH(CH3)2 + O2 -> C6H5-C(CH3)2-OOH ; C6H5-C(CH3)2-OOH + H2O(dil. H2SO4) -> C6H5OH + CH3COCH3
named.cond: Step 1: air oxidation. Step 2: dilute acid hydrolysis
named.tip: Write both steps; name acetone as the useful by-product, not just phenol.

named.name: Dow's process (phenol from chlorobenzene)
named.eq: C6H5Cl + 2NaOH -> C6H5-O-Na + NaCl + H2O ; C6H5-O-Na + HCl -> C6H5OH + NaCl
named.cond: fused with NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, then acidified
named.tip: Mention high temperature and pressure; product obtained as sodium phenoxide first, then acidified to phenol.

named.name: Phenol from diazonium salt (hydrolysis)
named.eq: C6H5-N2+ Cl- + H2O -> C6H5OH + N2 + HCl
named.tip: Byproduct is N2 gas, commonly forgotten in balancing.

named.name: Williamson's synthesis (ether formation)
named.cond: SN2 mechanism, works best with primary R'-X
named.tip: Use a primary halide; tertiary halide gives elimination (alkene) instead of ether - common trap question.

named.name: Fischer esterification
named.tip: Reaction is reversible; excess acid/alcohol and removing water drives equilibrium to ester side.

named.name: Dehydration of alcohol to alkene
named.tip: Follows Saytzeff's rule for unsymmetrical alcohols; tertiary > secondary > primary in ease of dehydration.

named.name: Dehydration of alcohol to ether
named.cond: conc. H2SO4, 413 K, excess alcohol (intermolecular dehydration)
named.tip: Low temperature with excess alcohol gives ether; high temperature gives alkene - do not mix up the two conditions.

named.name: Lucas test
named.cond: conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2 (Lucas reagent), room temperature
named.tip: Tertiary gives turbidity instantly, secondary in about 5 min, primary needs heating - examiners check exact timing.

named.name: Oxidation of alcohols (to aldehyde/ketone/acid)
named.eq: CH3CH2OH --(PCC or mild KMnO4)--> CH3CHO --(KMnO4/K2Cr2O7)--> CH3COOH
named.cond: PCC for mild oxidation (stops at aldehyde); hot acidic KMnO4/K2Cr2O7 for full oxidation to acid
named.tip: Secondary alcohol oxidises only to ketone (no further oxidation); tertiary alcohol resists oxidation.

steps: step 1: CH3CH2OH + conc. H2SO4, heat at 443 K -> CH2=CH2 + H2O (intramolecular dehydration)
conversions.ans: Ethanol heated with conc. H2SO4 at 443 K undergoes dehydration to give ethene.

steps: step 1: CH3CH2OH + conc. H2SO4 (excess alcohol), 413 K -> CH3CH2-O-CH2CH3 + H2O (intermolecular dehydration)
conversions.ans: Two molecules of ethanol combine on heating with conc. H2SO4 at 413 K with excess alcohol to give diethyl ether.

conversions.q: Convert ethanol to ethyl chloride (ethyl halide)
steps: step 1: CH3CH2OH + HCl (anhydrous ZnCl2, Lucas reagent) -> CH3CH2Cl + H2O
conversions.ans: Treat ethanol with Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2) to directly get ethyl chloride.

steps: step 1: C6H5OH + NaOH -> C6H5-O-Na + H2O (sodium phenoxide formation)
step 2: C6H5-O-Na + CH3I -> C6H5-O-CH3 + NaI (Williamson's synthesis)
conversions.ans: Convert phenol to sodium phenoxide with NaOH, then react with methyl iodide (Williamson's synthesis) to get anisole.

steps: step 1: C6H5Cl + NaOH (fused, 623 K, 300 atm) -> C6H5-O-Na + NaCl + H2O (Dow's process)
conversions.ans: Chlorobenzene is fused with NaOH under high temperature/pressure (Dow's process) to give sodium phenoxide, which is acidified to phenol.

conversions.q: Convert ethanol to acetic acid (ethanoic acid)
steps: step 1: CH3CH2OH + KMnO4/H+ (hot, acidic) -> CH3COOH + H2O
conversions.ans: Hot acidified KMnO4 (or K2Cr2O7) oxidises ethanol completely through acetaldehyde to acetic acid.

steps: step 1: CH3COOH (from oxidation of ethanol) + CH3CH2OH + conc. H2SO4, reflux -> CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (Fischer esterification)
conversions.ans: Part of ethanol is oxidised to acetic acid, which is then esterified with remaining ethanol using conc. H2SO4 to give ethyl acetate.

steps: step 1: (CH3)2CH-OH + conc. H2SO4, heat at 443 K -> CH3-CH=CH2 + H2O (dehydration, follows Saytzeff's rule)
conversions.ans: Secondary alcohol propan-2-ol dehydrates readily on heating with conc. H2SO4 at 443 K to give propene.
